sections.heading: How Scoring Works
sections.content: Matches are played as two sets. Rankings are based on total games won, not on winning or losing the match.

example.title: Example:
lines: Player 1 wins Set 1 6–2 and loses Set 2 4–6

sections.heading: How Sets End
sections.content: Each set is played to 6 games. If the score reaches 6–5, one additional game is played to determine how the set ends.
bullets: If the leading player wins the next game, the set ends 7–5.
If the trailing player wins the next game, the set ends 6–6.

example.title: Example:
lines: Player A wins the next game → 7–5, set over.
Player B wins the next game → 6–6, set ends as a draw.

sections.heading: Maximum Possible Score
sections.content: Because matches consist of two sets and each set can end with a maximum of 7 games won, the highest possible total score in a match is 14 games.

example.title: Example:
lines: Total games won by the winner: 14

sections.heading: Reporting Your Score
sections.content: After your match, report your total games won in the appropriate month.

guidelines.title: Guidelines:
items: Scores must be recorded in the correct month.
Always report a score, even if your total is 0.

subsections.title: Forfeit Without Playing
bullets: If feasible, rescheduling is encouraged, even if the month has already passed.

subsections.title: Match Ends Early Due to Injury
subsections.content: You and your opponent may agree to record the score as-is or reschedule to finish the match.
subsections.note: If the injured player chooses to forfeit, the winner receives either 6 points or the number of games already won, whichever is higher.
